transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-09-29 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (KindredAI Head Infra), Liam O'Shea (Security Architect), Tara Gomez (ML Platform), Ben Cho (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick intake focused on how KindredAI can run Redwood Private inside their AWS environment across EU and US regions. Primary concerns: private endpoints, static egress IPs for allow-listing, KMS with customer-managed keys, transit gateway vs VPC peering, and pilot timeline. SE asked for throughput/latency goals and offered benchmarking plan.

Topics covered:
- Deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private) tradeoffs
- Network topology options (PrivateLink, TGW, VPC peering, NAT/GW)
- Data residency and multi-region constraints
- Security controls (KMS, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs)
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um, today we want to understand your networking posture and any blockers for a private deployment of redwood.
[00:12] Priya Nair: thanks maya, appreciate it. we run most infra in AWS, split between us-east-1 and eu-west-1. we also have a govcloud-ish account for a small set of customers but not for this pilot. main ask is that the model traffic never traverses the public internet and we need static egress ips for partner allowlists.
[00:28] Omar Patel: okay great, so two immediate items — private connectivity and static egress. do you currently use a transit gateway or are you primarily peering?
[00:38] Priya Nair: we use a transit gateway for core services, but some teams still do VPC peering for low-latency paths. also we have strict egress nat gateways with 1:1 elastic IPs for service allowlisting.
[00:53] Jules Rivera: quick clar — when you say static egress do you mean customer-managed NAT EIP, or you want redwood to guarantee an egress IP for our service?
[01:02] Liam O'Shea: we want to be able to tell partners and external data providers a fixed set of IPs to whitelist. if redwood is in our VPC via a PrivateLink endpoint we still need to know the egress destination for callbacks, telemetry, etc.
[01:18] Omar Patel: that makes sense. with Private deployment we can run the inference nodes in your VPC or attach via PrivateLink depending on your ops preference. if nodes run in your VPC you control egress. if we run in a customer-dedicated VPC and peer it, we can provide a set of stable egress IPs but that typically maps to NATs behind the dedicated tenancy — there are patterns.
[01:38] Tara Gomez: latency is a concern. our production SLO is p99 < 60ms for generation calls for short contexts, longer contexts can hit 2-300ms. we need an initial runbook to approximate what config (batching, kv cache, quantization) will hit that.
[01:56] Omar Patel: understood. for short contexts (<=512 tokens) on dedicated capacity we often see p95 around 20-40ms depending on model family and kernel. p99 can vary with burstiness, so we typically recommend local KV cache and client-side prefix caching for hot prompts. we'll propose a config.
[02:14] Ben Cho: pricing question — if we go private, what's the delta vs hosted? i'm expecting a sizeable uplift but need numbers for procurement.
[02:23] Maya Chen: yes, dedicated/private are higher. i'll send example pricing for a 3-month pilot and also a hosted fall-back estimate.
[02:30] Priya Nair: security controls — we require customer-managed KMS for any key encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key for telemetry obfuscation. how does redwood handle KMS/HSM?
[02:43] Jules Rivera: currently our Private offering supports customer KMS integration; we can either integrate with your AWS KMS key via IAM role or, for on-prem, use an HSM connector. we'll include the KMS integration guide in the doc share.
[02:58] Liam O'Shea: audit logs — we need event level logging for admin actions, model version rollouts, and access to raw requests for compliance. retention 12 months.
[03:10] Omar Patel: we have an audit pipeline that can forward logs to your S3 or CloudWatch with KMS encryption and a retention policy; retention is configurable. we'll share the schema and sample logs.
[03:23] Priya Nair: also data residency — certain customers require EU-only processing. can we gate models to region and also have region-aware routing?
[03:35] Maya Chen: yes — redwood supports region pinning and routing policies. common approach is to deploy inference nodes in both eu-west-1 and us-east-1 and route requests from eu tenants to the eu cluster. we can also set fallback rules.
[03:49] Tara Gomez: about connectivity options: you're mentioning PrivateLink and peering — which do you recommend for our scale? we anticipate 40 req/s initial, spiking to 200 req/s in peak tests.
[04:03] Omar Patel: for that scale, TGW with Transit VPC or shared services is easiest operationally. PrivateLink is great when you want strict service endpoints per VPC but can add management overhead if you have many consumer VPCs. VPC peering is simpler but doesn't scale well for many-to-many.
[04:20] Priya Nair: in our case TGW is standard. we need a diagram of how redwood would attach — whether via a TGW attachment or PrivateLink endpoint.
[04:29] Maya Chen: we'll include both diagrams: TGW attachment and PrivateLink + NLB inside your account.
[04:36] Ben Cho: procurement hold — contract terms need standard indemnity and data processing addendum. is redwood up for our standard DPA?
[04:45] Maya Chen: yes we have a DPA template and enterprise legal has gone through similar ones. i'll attach the DPA and enterprise contract addenda.
[04:54] Liam O'Shea: network ports and egress — we need a minimal port list and sample security groups. also how we handle DNS — will redwood place private records in our private hosted zone?
[05:05] Jules Rivera: common pattern: we create PrivateLink endpoints and you create an internal AWS NLB target group. For DNS we can add internal records to your private hosted zone or you can CNAME to the endpoint. we'll include exact port and SG recommendations.
[05:18] Priya Nair: backups and snapshots — if the model KV cache contains derivatives of customer prompts, do you persist that in EBS snapshots in our account? what's the retention and encryption?
[05:29] Omar Patel: we typically keep KV caches in ephemeral EBS volumes when running in your VPC; by default they are encrypted with your KMS. persistence is optional; for compliance we can disable long-term snapshots.
[05:42] Maya Chen: question for you priya — what's your target timeline to have a pilot running?
[05:48] Priya Nair: ideally pilot in 6 weeks. we have budget cycle next month and security sign-off could take 3-4 weeks. procurement would prefer a 3-month pilot.
[05:57] Tara Gomez: success criteria — functional correctness, throughput 100 req/s sustained with p95 < 80ms, p99 < 200ms for 8k contexts, and zero data egress to third-party regions for EU customers.
[06:13] Omar Patel: noted. we'll put together a benchmark plan and target configs.
[06:19] Ben Cho: one blocker might be IP allowlist for partners — do you need our partners to whitelist redwood egress?
[06:25] Maya Chen: yes we can provide an allowlist. if you want redwood to egress through your NATs, that solves the problem; otherwise we can provide static IPs from our dedicated tenancy. we'll enumerate both options.
[06:40] Liam O'Shea: are there any known limitations — e.g., models that don't support quantized kernels and hence increase latency?
[06:47] Omar Patel: some model families at high quantization levels can impact quality/latency; we'll outline recommended model variants and quantization profiles. also for very low latency you might want dedicated capacity pinned to a topology.
[07:00] Priya Nair: curious about upgrades/rollouts — we need canary and immediate rollback hooks if a new model regresses.
[07:08] Jules Rivera: Redwood Console supports canaries and automatic rollback policies tied to evals. we can show an example during the deep technical walkthrough.
[07:18] Maya Chen: okay, do we have any immediate red flags?
[07:20] Liam O'Shea: none immediate, just need to validate KMS integration and the egress model.
[07:24] Priya Nair: and final note — we may require an on-prem connector later for an EU sovereign customer but that is post-pilot.
[07:34] Omar Patel: noted. we can discuss on-prem HSM connectors in follow-up.
[07:40] Maya Chen: great. i'll recap next steps at the end.
[07:44] (discussion continues with specific port numbers and sample CIDRs, some cross talk and clarifications)
[18:12] Omar Patel: for the benchmark plan, i'd like to collect some sample traffic patterns — average tokens per request, distribution of short vs long contexts, and percent of streaming vs unary calls. tara can you send an export?
[18:27] Tara Gomez: yes i'll pull a week of traffic and obfuscate any PII, send to the shared drive.
[18:35] Maya Chen: i'll attach a draft network diagram and checklist to the crm activity — link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/kindredai-private-onramp (note: placeholder link)
[18:45] Priya Nair: we'll confirm TGW attachment window and provide CIDRs by next tuesday.
[18:51] Ben Cho: procurement wants a simple statement of work and pilot pricing, send that please.
[19:00] Maya Chen: will do. final recap: 1) redwood to send network diagrams (TGW + PrivateLink), KMS integration docs, SOC2/ISO reports, and pilot pricing. 2) Kindred to share VPC CIDRs, sample traffic, and confirm timeline for TGW attachment. 3) schedule deep technical session with security and infra — target early October.
[19:20] Liam O'Shea: thanks all, that covers it.
[19:23] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
